notes: Total 100 pieces: b1-b76 plus 4 leg copies of 6 pieces each (24) = 100, which matches the parts list.
The manual is stud-stacking pictures. Where the exact stud under a piece is not clear, I gave a plausible join and left the ports null.

The booklet builds two sub-models (the sheep and the base) that are combined in the final picture. The leg brackets (15672) of the sheep stand on the green plates of the base, so I joined them there (assumed stud fit). The manual shows no numbered step for it, so this is an assumption.
The Envelope (b39) is an inventory item that is not built into the model. It has a contact edge to the base (b40) only so that it is not an isolated node.
Body: b4 (Technic brick) is placed on b1 in a flipped view. The exact stacking of the tan bricks, b9 and b14 on b3 and of b16 on top is approximate.

Head: b24 and b25 (87087) are assumed to be the two bricks that carry the eye tiles on their side studs. b22 sits on b21, and the clip plate b35 clips onto the handle b20. There is also a contact edge b20-b22. This is an assumption.

Legs are one repeat built 4 times (steps 12 and 13). Each leg pivots on one of the four body pins b5, b6, b10, b11 through its Technic brick hole. There is also a contact edge between each leg's Technic brick and the body plate b16.
Base: p1=b40, p2=b45, p3=b50. The blue brick b44 bridges p1 and p2. The placement of the 3037 slopes (b46-b49), the end slopes and the green tiles and plates is approximated from isometric views.
The tail pin b37 (4274) goes into b4's pin hole, and the plate b38 pushes onto the pin end.
